FIELD REFERENCE

Lake sturgeon (Acipenser fulvescens): size, age, range

The lake sturgeon is Acipenser fulvescens, one of the largest freshwater fish in North America. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service says adults are usually 4 to 6 feet long and 30 to 80 pounds, and live 50 to 100 years. It has a shark-like tail and bony plates, and it lives on the bottom of large lakes and rivers.

Updated 2026-11-21 · Castward

What is a lake sturgeon?

Key factDetail
Scientific nameAcipenser fulvescens
How to identify itShark-like tail, a covering of bony plates, and four whisker-like barbels in front of a toothless mouth that extends to suck up food
Typical adult size4 to 6 feet and 30 to 80 pounds (U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service)
Largest fishAbout 7 feet and 200 to 300 pounds (U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service). FishBase records a maximum length of 274 cm and a maximum published weight of 125 kg
Life spanUsually 50 to 100 years; the oldest reach about 150 years. FishBase records a maximum reported age of 152 years
First spawningAt 10 to 30 years old, and not every year
RangeSt. Lawrence, Hudson Bay, Great Lakes, Mississippi River and Coosa River watersheds: five Canadian provinces and 24 U.S. states
HabitatThe bottom of large lakes and rivers, usually in 5 to 9 metres of water over mud, sand and gravel (FishBase). It moves into rocky, fast river water to spawn
FoodSnails, crayfish, mussels and aquatic insects; sometimes small fish and eggs

What should you know about lake sturgeon?

How big do lake sturgeon get?

The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service says the largest and oldest fish grow to about 7 feet and 200 to 300 pounds. A typical adult is 4 to 6 feet and 30 to 80 pounds.

How long do lake sturgeon live?

Typical adults live 50 to 100 years, and the oldest reach about 150 years, according to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. FishBase records a maximum reported age of 152 years.

Where do lake sturgeon live?

They live in the St. Lawrence, Hudson Bay, Great Lakes, Mississippi River and Coosa River watersheds. In Canada that covers Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Ontario and Quebec. In the United States the range crosses 24 states.

Do lake sturgeon live only in lakes?

No. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service says they do well in lakes and in rivers. Adults move into large rivers to lay eggs over gravel, cobble and boulders in fast water.

What do lake sturgeon eat?

They feed on the bottom. Four barbels help them find snails, crayfish, mussels and aquatic insects, and sometimes small fish and eggs. They have no teeth and suck food up with an extendable mouth.

Can you fish for lake sturgeon?

Only where and when the state or province allows it. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service says harvest is heavily regulated and monitored. Rules differ by water and can prohibit harvest, so read the rules of the fisheries agency for the exact water and date.

Is the lake sturgeon an endangered species?

The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service species record shows a finding of April 23, 2024 that a federal listing was not warranted. States and provinces set their own protection. Check the agency for your water.
